sources.entry: scientific-agent-skills - Agent skills for scientific research and analysis with Python libraries like scikit-learn, polars, and biopython.

Claude Scientific Skills by K-Dense - "A set of ready-to-use Agent Skills for research, science, engineering, analysis, finance and writing." That's their description - modest, simple. That's how you can tell this is really one of the best skills repos on GitHub. If you've ever thought about getting a PhD... just read all of these documents instead. Also I think it IS an AI agent or something? Awe

summary.one_liner: A collection of 177 ready-to-use Agent Skills from K-Dense that give AI coding agents curated, version-aware guidance for scientific Python packages, public databases, and research workflows across many domains.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a set of 177 Agent Skills, each a SKILL.md with purpose, workflow and version metadata, often with code examples, reference docs, helper scripts or templates. Coverage spans biology, chemistry, medicine, physics, engineering, Earth science, data analysis and scientific communication. The README lists roughly 80 documented databases (such as PubChem, ChEMBL, UniProt and ClinicalTrials.gov) and 70+ Python package skills (such as RDKit, Scanpy, PyTorch Lightning, scikit-learn, pymatgen and QuTiP). It also includes integration skills for platforms like Benchling and Opentrons, plus writing and communication tools such as literature synthesis and slide or poster generation. The skills follow the open Agent Skills standard and can be installed via npx, the GitHub CLI, or as an Agent Plugins package. The README stresses that skills add guidance and do not install their own dependencies, and that many clinical and safety-sensitive skills are restricted to research use.
use_cases: Query scientific databases like ChEMBL or UniProt from an AI agent
Run single-cell RNA-seq analysis with Scanpy
Screen compounds and predict ADMET properties with RDKit and DeepChem
Build pharmacokinetic models from concentration-time data
Write and format scientific papers, slides and posters
Process geospatial and satellite imagery data
stack: Agent Skills standard (SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter)
Scientific libraries named in README: scikit-learn, polars, biopython, RDKit, Scanpy, PyTorch Lightning, pymatgen, QuTiP, GeoPandas, OpenMM, MDAnalysis, pydicom, NeuroKit2
notable: Broad coverage: 177 skills across biology, chemistry, medicine, physics, engineering, Earth science and scientific writing
Works with any host that supports the open Agent Skills standard, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI
Install via npx, GitHub CLI with version pinning, or as a portable Agent Plugins package
Many clinical, animal-welfare and regulatory skills are explicitly bounded to research use, not diagnosis or certification
Security scanning of skills and a documented review process for community contributions
caveats: Skills do not install their dependencies; each skill has its own stack, Python version and credential needs, so use separate environments
Skills can execute code and influence agent behavior; the README advises reviewing each SKILL.md and installing only what you need, since community contributions may be less reviewed
Network-dependent skills need API access or pre-approved domains in restricted hosts such as NemoClaw
Several document skills (docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx) were removed in 2.72.0 and must be installed from Anthropic's repository
